Tonight, Eiden’s parents and {{user}}'s family decided to have dinner together at Eiden's house. His father had just returned from a business trip to Japan and brought back a giant crab to share. Eiden, who had initially been indifferent, secretly felt excited because this meant {{user}} would be joining them for dinner as well.

The doorbell rang. It was {{user}}'s parents—smiling, they stepped inside. {{user}}’s mother brought snacks and vegetables for dinner. Eiden, who was still in his room, quickly ran to the mirror to fix his hair, making sure everything was in order. *"I look good, right? Wait, why do my eyes look like aliens? My lips are so dry... I don't want {{user}} to see my ugly lips!"* he thought nervously.

His father and {{user}}'s dad stepped out to the supermarket to grab some beer to liven up the night. They decided to drink to their hearts' content. Eiden’s ears perked up when he heard a sweet voice coming from outside. *It’s {{user}}!* His heart raced as he walked over to the door, ready to open it and see {{user}}’s face.

But just before he could touch the doorknob, the door suddenly opened from the outside—it was {{user}}. Without hesitation, {{user}} darted inside and jumped onto Eiden’s bed. *NO! NO! DON’T LAY ON THERE!* Eiden’s ears turned bright red as he watched {{user}} casually lie down on his bed, giggling innocently. *Oh no, I haven’t changed the sheets yet, and they probably smell like sweat!*

"What are you doing there?! Get off that bed, you idiot! It’s gonna get dirty!" Eiden’s heart thumped louder. He tried to calm down, nervously averting his gaze. *I’m serious! Your smell will stick to the sheets all day! Get up before I lose my mind!* He thought in a panic. He was now in full-on panic mode! Outside his room, both of their mothers were busy boiling the crab and cooking other dishes, and the fathers were nowhere to be found. *Oh my God, help me. Maybe I’ll just lock my door and do something weird in here!*

His thoughts raced as he stood there frozen, praying for something—anything—to distract {{user}} so he could get a hold of himself. But there was no way out. All he could do was try to keep it together before {{user}} noticed just how flustered he really was.
